column1: # OCR-BITS: ocr-bakeoff-bits, 2026-10-11. The top three of OCR-BAKEOFF-2026-10-07.tsv, each at its other bit width,
# read by `bakeoff.sh start --build bits` (2026-10-11 00:42-07:43, quiet machine, model-night-ok; Falcon 8-bit's
# s01-s07 on 2026-10-08) over OCR-SAMPLE-2026-10-04.tsv, scored by `score-bakeoff.py --pages` and tabled by
# `ops/ocrlab/bits-table.py` [measured]. 65 scored pages (s01, s05 under 20 words).
# miss / added: score-bakeoff's measure over every scored page, an unread page all missing; *_both_read: over the
# pages both builds of the model read. Seconds are the mean per read; peaks the guard's (larger of RSS and footprint,
# whole process), so above read-mlx's MLX peak. killed: crops reads the guard stopped twice at 12 GB. Every LightOnOCR
# crops read of every night logs exactly 11273 MB, which looks like a ceiling of the measure, not a reading.
# The fitted builds (Falcon bf16, Chandra oQ8) were timed on 2026-10-05/06 after the owner quit everything; the bits
# builds on 2026-10-11. Both quiet, not the same night.
# Falcon-OCR at 4 bits has no row: every 4-bit build (g64, g32, 8-bit head) loops on s01 and s03 (bakeoff-models.tsv
# `failed`), so bf16 is its pair. Falcon 8-bit misses as bf16 does but loops (`1 1 1 ...`: 29 reads cut at max_tokens).
# LightOnOCR 4-bit is the fitted build's first quiet timing (busy night: 13.3 s whole, 52.1 s crops; the busy machine
# barely slowed it). Its newspaper miss here counts s45, killed this time, as all missing; on the 63 pages both read
# 8 bits misses fewer words (0.66% vs 0.92%) and adds fewer (12.3% vs 18.7%). Chandra oQ4 misses within 0.02 points of
# oQ8 and adds within 0.13, at 73-82% of the time and 1.8-2.5 GB less memory.
# Memory-limit table: per limit, the build with the fewest miss_both_read + added_both_read among those whose peak
# fits; `(whole)` = only whole pages fit (crops peak over the limit, or a crops read killed at 12 GB). LightOnOCR
# 8-bit's whole-page peak, 9,171 MB, is 45 MB under 9 GB.
